cards.text: Job just poured out his pain to his friends and to God. Now Bildad the Shuhite, one of the three friends who came to comfort him (Job 2:11), takes his turn. And he opens with, "How long will you go on saying such things?" Friend, that's not a warm-up. That's the oven already blazing.

cards.question: Bildad asks Job how long he'll go on saying such things. What does Bildad say the words of Job's mouth are like?

cards.text: A blustering wind. Friend, Bildad just told a hurting man he sounds like a leaf blower at 7 a.m. on a Saturday.

cards.question: Bildad asks, "Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty pervert what is right?" With these questions, Bildad is saying God never twists what is right.

cards.text: Then Bildad goes somewhere I'd tiptoe around. He brings up Job's children, who died when a mighty wind struck the house they were in (Job 1:18-19).

cards.question: Bildad brings up Job's children. What does he say God did when they sinned against Him?

answers.text: He gave them over to their rebellion
He gave them one more warning
He sent them far away from home

cards.text: Then Bildad turns to Job himself. And here come the ifs.

cards.question: Bildad says if Job would earnestly seek God, what should Job ask the Almighty for?
Bildad adds another if. If Job is pure and upright, even now God will rouse Himself on Job's behalf and ___ his righteous estate.
Bildad tells Job that if all this happens, Job's latter days will be smaller than his beginnings.

cards.text: Modest beginnings? Job had seven thousand sheep and three thousand camels (Job 1:3). Friend, I came with a 25 cent sticker on me, so trust me, THAT'S modest.
Next Bildad tells Job where to look for answers: "Please inquire of past generations and consider the discoveries of their fathers."

cards.question: Why does Bildad tell Job to ask the past generations?

answers.text: We know little and our days are short
They saw God face to face
They lived in better times than ours

cards.text: Born yesterday. Not YOU were born yesterday. WE. Bildad climbs right into the crib with everybody else.

cards.question: Bildad says the past generations have nothing to teach Job.

cards.text: Now Bildad switches to pictures from nature. He asks if papyrus grows where there is no marsh, and if reeds flourish without water.

cards.question: Bildad's papyrus and reeds need water. Without it, what happens to them while the shoots are still uncut?

answers.text: They dry up faster than grass

cards.text: Drying up with nothing to keep you going. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer with no light, so I am a CERTIFIED expert in drying up.

cards.question: Bildad says drying up like that is the destiny of all who ___ God, and the hope of the godless will perish.

cards.text: Bildad keeps going about the godless man. His confidence is fragile, Bildad says.

cards.question: Bildad says the godless man's confidence is fragile. Where does he say that man's security is?

cards.text: He leans on his web, but it gives way. That's leaning way back in the office chair you KNOW has been making that noise.
Then a new picture. Bildad says, "He is a well-watered plant in the sunshine, spreading its shoots over the garden," with roots wrapped around the rock heap, looking for a home among the stones.

cards.question: Bildad says if the well-watered plant is uprooted, its place will welcome it back.

cards.text: Uprooted, and the place says, "I never saw you." Friend, I KNOW that one. One day I'm on the counter, the next a shiny new stamper is in my spot like I was never there.

cards.question: Bildad calls all this the joy of his way. Then what does Bildad say will spring from the dust?

cards.text: Now Bildad wraps it up with "Behold," which is Bible for EVERYBODY LOOK OVER HERE.

cards.question: Bildad says God does not ___ the blameless, nor will He strengthen the hand of evildoers.
Bildad ends with hope for Job. What does Bildad say God will yet fill Job's mouth with?
Bildad says Job's enemies will be clothed in honor.

cards.text: That's Bildad's last word, with the tent of the wicked no more. And trust me, friend, this conversation is NOT done.
